text:
maria: Quick Q — for the payments service gateway, should we do ALB TLS termination (L7) or NLB passthrough + pod TLS (L4)? Thinking about healthchecks, secret rotation, and terraform diffs.

aj: I favour ALB termination for app-level routing and simpler certs, but health checks get weird if app only speaks TLS.

kevin: +1 ALB for path-based routing. If you terminate at ALB you can offload certs to ACM and avoid rotating pods' secrets. downside: can't do mTLS easily.

maria: Right. We need mutual TLS for internal between services though. payments->billing needs mTLS. Could do ALB edge TLS + mTLS internally (sidecar or certs in pod). How would secret rotation look?

sam: For rotation I'd prefer cert-manager issuing pod certs (CA signed) mounted via CSI driver. That way ALB uses ACM cert (managed) and pods get rotated certs automatically. Terraform only manages ALB + ACM association — not the per-pod cert lifecycle.

aj: That matches my thinking. If you go NLB passthrough and terminate in pod you can use ACM on NLB (listener with cert ARN) or the pods need certs. But NLB TLS termination means you still wire cert ARN in terraform creating the lb listener. That moves rotation to infra side.

maria: We need a proposal I can link in the PR. Can someone paste a minimal k8s svc/annotation example for ALB vs NLB so I can show what the terraform diff looks like?

kevin: ALB (using aws-load-balancer-controller) example:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  annotations:
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme: internet-facing
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/listen-ports: '[{"HTTP":80},{"HTTPS":443}]'
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/certificate-arn: arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:111:certificate/xxxx
spec:
  rules:
    - http:
        paths:
          - path: /payments/*
            backend:
              service:
                name: payments-svc
                port:
                  number: 8080
```
Note: aws-load-balancer-controller maps certs from the annotation and we manage the ACM cert via terraform (aws_acm_certificate, aws_acm_certificate_validation).

sam: NLB passthrough svc example (k8s svc type=LoadBalancer):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: payments-svc
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: nlb
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-cert: arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:111:certificate/xxxx
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: tcp
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
    - port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
      protocol: TCP
  selector:
    app: payments
```
With NLB TLS listener, cert rotation is infra-driven (you update the cert ARN in terraform or use ACM auto-renewal + aliasing), pods see raw TCP. Health checks: set target-type ip and health check port to 8080 or use TCP health checks.

maria: Good. Healthcheck behaviour for ALB: ALB can do HTTP health check at /health even if front TLS is terminated. For NLB TLS passthrough we may need a separate health port or use TCP health checks which are less expressive.

aj: Exactly. If payments needs to return 200/404 semantics for readiness, ALB HTTP check is nicer. NLB forces us to expose an unencrypted health endpoint or rely on sidecar to answer TCP.

kevin: One gotcha: when using ALB and header-based routing we must ensure X-Forwarded-Proto or TLS info is preserved so app can build correct redirects. The controller handles that but app config must trust the proxy.

maria: About secrets wiring — if we choose ALB termination + pod mTLS: suggested setup = ACM for ALB (managed in terraform), cert-manager issuing short-lived certs for pods (mounted via CSI + backed by Secrets Manager or k8s secrets). Any objections?

sam: Works for me. For secrets storage I recommend Secrets Manager for rotation auditability and then CSI driver to mount into pods. cert-manager can sign via a private CA stored in AWS Secrets Manager or use vault. Avoid long-lived static k8s secrets.

aj: Also consider using the service-account-based cert rotation for sidecars (SPIRE) if we want stronger identity, but that's more infra work.

maria: For terraform changes I'll include:
- aws_lb + aws_lb_listener (if we manage ALB outside K8s) OR aws_lb for NLB with listener + certificate ARN
- aws_acm_certificate and aws_acm_certificate_validation for ACM certs (ALB path)
- aws_secretsmanager_secret for CA/key if we manage our own CA
- k8s service/ingress objects kept minimal: ingress -> ALB annotations; svc->nlb annotations

aj: If possible keep ACM cert resource in the same module as the k8s ingress module so plan shows clear link. If teams prefer infra PR separate, document the ordering: create ACM cert -> validate -> update ingress/service annotation -> controller picks it up.

kevin: We should also add an automated smoke test in deploy pipeline: after rollout, request /health via curl (with SNI) and verify 200. Helps catch header/trust issues. deploy-bot can post results.

deploy-bot: Reminder: when updating load balancer cert ARN, plan may show replacement of listener. Schedule changes during maintenance window to avoid connection drops.

maria: Awesome — I'll draft the PR using ALB termination + cert-manager for pod mTLS, and add a fallback doc for NLB passthrough in case we need raw TCP. I'll link terraform snippets and the k8s yaml from above. Thanks all :heart:

kevin: LGTM. One more: include how we're rotating the CA for pod certs — rolling restart window and pre-warm new CA cert in secrets so pods don't fail auth.

maria: Will do. I'll post the PR link once ready.
